hints: Apply Newton's second law in the horizontal direction: driving force minus resistance equals mass times acceleration.
Substitute $m = 4000\text{ kg}$, resistance $= 900\text{ N}$, and $a = 0.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law in the forward direction of motion:
$$F_D - R = ma$$
$$F_D - 900 = 4000(0.5)$$
$$F_D - 900 = 2000$$

Solve for the driving force $F_D$:
$$F_D = 2000 + 900 = 2900\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Identify the horizontal forces acting on the minibus: a forward driving force $F_D$ produced by the engine and a backward resistive force $R = 900\text{ N}$.

State Newton's second law for linear motion:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma$$
$$F_D - R = ma$$

Substitute the minibus mass $m = 4000\text{ kg}$, resistance $R = 900\text{ N}$, and acceleration $a = 0.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$F_D - 900 = 4000 \times 0.5$$
$$F_D - 900 = 2000$$

Add $900$ to both sides to solve for $F_D$:
$$F_D = 2000 + 900 = 2900\text{ N}$$

hints: At constant speed, acceleration is zero, so the driving force equals the resistance force ($F_D = 900\text{ N}$).
Use the power formula $P = F_D v$ with $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
Because the minibus travels at constant speed, acceleration is zero, so the driving force balances the resistance force:
$$F_D = 900\text{ N}$$

Calculate the power using $P = F_D v$:
$$P = 900 \times 25 = 22500\text{ W} = 22.5\text{ kW}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
When a vehicle moves at a constant speed along a horizontal road, its acceleration is zero:
$$a = 0 \implies F_{\text{net}} = 0$$
Therefore, the driving force must equal the resistance force:
$$F_D = R = 900\text{ N}$$

State the relationship between mechanical power, driving force, and velocity:
$$P = F_D \times v$$

Substitute $F_D = 900\text{ N}$ and constant speed $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 900 \times 25 = 22500\text{ W}$$

Divide by $1000$ to express the power in kilowatts:
$$P = \frac{22500}{1000} = 22.5\text{ kW}$$
